questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Personal interest in the destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the adminstration was helpful, but quite busy during intro weeks, so communication was not very efficent. Had some trouble with the course registration, and had to wait for response on email more than a week.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information per mail.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was fairly easy but expensive to rent outside of the official student housing organization (SiO). The best option if not renting a room or shared apartment through SiO is to look on
Finn.no
, kind of like
dba.dk
. But expect high rents.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not really any student accommodation on campus or next to it, so even if you rent through SiO, the official organization for student housing, they have several locations around the city. Electricity/heating is included if renting through sio, but not necessarily if you rent privately. Be aware of this since those bills can be quite big in the winter.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You cant have pets at any of the SiO student housing. Hence it made it more troublesome for me to find housing since I have a dog.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall all to limited course choices and flexibility in what courses you can take as a Scandinavian exchange student.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to choose courses from a specific list of courses available to exchange students – these were all courses given in English. Since I speak Swedish and a bit I expected it to be possible for me to also choose from courses given in Norwegian. This was in theory possible but in practice very complicated. A lot of courses were tied to specific programs and were not possible to choose as an exchange students.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus coordinator and coordinator at different departments helped me through the process of finding courses that suited me since my initial choices were not all available in the end.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of the courses I wanted to take was not available in that semester as it turned out. They updated the course list very late I would say, so when time came for me to register, most of the courses I had set my eyes on were not even available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the courses shown in the course lists online might not all be available when the time comes for registering. If you are Scandinavian speaking, do ask if there is the possibility to take courses given in Norwegian, if you don't find suiting courses among those offered to exchange students in English.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In the end, the two courses I took were interesting and of good quality teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was adequate to MA I would say based on my experience from KU. Some readings were challenging, but lectures were easy to follow. Exams was easy to pass but A grades required a solid performance.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The futures of work
Achieving the SDGs: Global goals and national interests

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The futures of work - in the field of human geography, very interesting, and makes you reflect on your own future of work. Inspiring professor teaching the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Electricity/heating. My apartment was heated by electric radiator which was unexpected for me. Since prices for electricy sky-rocketed in the winter of my stay it meant a unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Going out for drinks/eating/cultural events is expensive and also buying food at supermarket. Overall I felt poorer in Oslo compared to Copenhagen.

Training activites was very affordable through the student organization SiO.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I signed up for SiO Athletica membership (around 170 dkk per month) and that gives you access to several gyms and swimming hall around the city, and you can book classes for yoga etc. without extra cost. Also you can rent skiing equipment very affordable in the winter from SiO.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot going on in various student organisation but I did not explore much of that. My impression was that in general people are a bit younger at UiO compared to KU. Since im 32 I did not feel attracted to much of the student parties and gatherings going on partly for that reason.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Nature is amazing around Oslo. Go for hikes, skiing, go out to the islands. There is a lot to explore if you are an active person.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Holmenkollen. Grefsenkollen. Check out parks and hang out in Töyen- Torshov - Sagene - Grunerlökka, in my opinion the most interesting and fun areas to hang around in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Since I am Swedish it is not much of a difference. I would say its like a mix of Sweden and America in a weird way. To generalize: Norwegians are more introverted than danes and more obsessed with material wealth and gadgets. They are very friendly and easy going once you speak to them however,

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: try to befriend other exchange students early on so you have a social network from the start. expect it to take some time to get to know locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are less outgoing compared to copenhagen. Nightlife and fast food is much more limited and more expensive.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Dog culture is very relaxed, people go with their dogs without leash and there are a lot of parks to recreate with other dogs and dogowners. (relevant for me since I have a dog. Art scene is small but vibrant.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Oslo is expensive and bit boring
- Nature is great
- Academic culture more or less the same

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you look for accomodation try to find something fairly central. Avoid Nydalen and Storo, horrible areas in my opinion.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing a new city. Get a sense of the similarities and differences between Norwegian culture and Danish and Swedish culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding friends and social activities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Wheater in Oslo is in general much better than Copenhagen. Not particularly windy and a lot of sun! And proper winter with snow.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
